min_knee_angle.name: Smallest knee angle
min_knee_angle.calculation: Minimum 2D shooting-side knee angle over valid frames. Angle between the two limb segments in the image plane using pixel-scaled MediaPipe landmarks. The pipeline requires all three landmarks to pass its visibility check.
min_knee_angle.reliability_indicator: Sufficient knee coverage and ordered shot events
min_knee_angle.supported_interpretation: How bent the knee appeared at its most bent point
min_knee_angle.unsupported_interpretation: Ideal form, shooting effectiveness, force, power, or cause of a miss

knee_angle_range.name: Knee angle change across the shot
knee_angle_range.calculation: Maximum minus minimum 2D knee angle over valid frames. Angle between the two limb segments in the image plane using pixel-scaled MediaPipe landmarks. The pipeline requires all three landmarks to pass its visibility check.
knee_angle_range.reliability_indicator: Sufficient knee coverage and ordered shot events
knee_angle_range.supported_interpretation: Size of the measured knee angle range
knee_angle_range.unsupported_interpretation: Ideal form, shooting effectiveness, force, power, or cause of a miss, movement direction or speed

release_elbow_angle.name: Elbow angle at estimated release
release_elbow_angle.calculation: 2D shoulder–elbow–wrist joint angle at the estimated release frame. Angle between the two limb segments in the image plane using pixel-scaled MediaPipe landmarks. The pipeline requires all three landmarks to pass its visibility check.
release_elbow_angle.reliability_indicator: Sufficient elbow coverage, ordered shot events and any required release-frame value
release_elbow_angle.supported_interpretation: How bent the shooting elbow appeared in that frame
release_elbow_angle.unsupported_interpretation: Ideal form, shooting effectiveness, force, power, or cause of a miss, ball launch angle

max_elbow_angle.name: Largest elbow angle
max_elbow_angle.calculation: Maximum 2D elbow angle from start to the earlier of end and six frames after release. Angle between the two limb segments in the image plane using pixel-scaled MediaPipe landmarks. The pipeline requires all three landmarks to pass its visibility check.
max_elbow_angle.reliability_indicator: Sufficient elbow coverage, ordered shot events and any required release-frame value
max_elbow_angle.supported_interpretation: Straightest visible elbow position in that window
max_elbow_angle.unsupported_interpretation: Ideal form, shooting effectiveness, force, power, or cause of a miss

elbow_angle_range.name: Elbow angle range
elbow_angle_range.calculation: Maximum minus minimum 2D elbow angle in the maximum-elbow window. Angle between the two limb segments in the image plane using pixel-scaled MediaPipe landmarks. The pipeline requires all three landmarks to pass its visibility check.
elbow_angle_range.reliability_indicator: Sufficient elbow coverage, ordered shot events and any required release-frame value
elbow_angle_range.supported_interpretation: Size of the measured elbow angle range
elbow_angle_range.unsupported_interpretation: Ideal form, shooting effectiveness, force, power, or cause of a miss

elbow_extension_after_release.name: Elbow straightening after estimated release
elbow_extension_after_release.calculation: Maximum 2D elbow angle from estimated release through the early follow-through window minus release elbow angle. Angle between the two limb segments in the image plane using pixel-scaled MediaPipe landmarks. The pipeline requires all three landmarks to pass its visibility check.
elbow_extension_after_release.reliability_indicator: Sufficient elbow coverage, ordered shot events and any required release-frame value
elbow_extension_after_release.supported_interpretation: How much farther the elbow straightened during that measured window
elbow_extension_after_release.unsupported_interpretation: Ideal form, shooting effectiveness, force, power, or cause of a miss, how long the arm stayed up or what the wrist did

shooting_motion_ms.name: Time from detected start to estimated release
shooting_motion_ms.calculation: Stored estimated release time minus detected start time
shooting_motion_ms.reliability_indicator: Pipeline quality pass and ordered shot events
shooting_motion_ms.unsupported_interpretation: Total shot duration, power, or confirmed release timing

knee_coverage_pct.name: Knee tracking coverage
knee_coverage_pct.calculation: 100 × valid knee frames divided by expected frames
knee_coverage_pct.supported_interpretation: Share of frames with an angle

elbow_coverage_pct.name: Elbow tracking coverage
elbow_coverage_pct.calculation: 100 × valid elbow frames divided by expected frames
elbow_coverage_pct.supported_interpretation: Share of frames with an angle

tracking_coverage_pct.name: Ball tracking coverage
tracking_coverage_pct.calculation: 100 × tracked frame count divided by inclusive span of tracked frames
tracking_coverage_pct.phase: first through last tracked ball frame
tracking_coverage_pct.supported_interpretation: How often the tracker supplied a position in its observed span
tracking_coverage_pct.unsupported_interpretation: Tracking accuracy, uninterrupted flight, release speed or power

scoring.principle: In the NBA a made free throw is worth one point. A made field goal is worth two from on or inside the three-point line, and three from outside.
scoring.use_when: When the question is about scoring rules.
scoring.avoid_when: When asked about an individual shooting result.

free_throw.principle: A free throw is an undefended attempt from the free-throw line. A successful attempt is worth one point.
free_throw.use_when: When the question asks what a free throw is.
free_throw.avoid_when: When the player asks for a free-throw practice drill.

stance.principle: A comfortable base helps you start each shot balanced.
stance.cue: Set both feet before you lift the ball and feel your weight centered.
stance.purpose: Start each rep from a stable position.
stance.use_when: When the setup feels rushed or unstable.
stance.avoid_when: When a comfortable, repeatable stance is already working.
stance.progression: Take a short set from one spot. Reset your feet before each rep.
stance.evaluation: Check whether your setup feels repeatable. Record makes separately.
stance.source: USA Basketball — 7 Tips To Improve Your Shooting Mechanics

preparation.principle: A repeatable ball position gives your shooting hand a consistent start.
preparation.cue: Start with the ball comfortably in front of you and let your shooting hand sit under it.
preparation.purpose: Make the lift easier to repeat.
preparation.use_when: When the player is learning the pickup or grip.
preparation.avoid_when: When changing the pickup would add another focus to the current practice.
preparation.progression: From close range, rehearse the lift, then take a short set at normal speed.
preparation.evaluation: Check whether the ball starts in a similar place across reps.
preparation.source: USA Basketball — 7 Tips To Improve Your Shooting Mechanics

knees.principle: A comfortable knee bend can help you find a repeatable setup.
knees.cue: Let your knees soften slightly before you lift the ball.
knees.purpose: Keep the setup comfortable and repeatable.
knees.use_when: When testing a more repeatable preparation.
knees.avoid_when: When deeper bending causes discomfort or the player already has a reliable setup.
knees.progression: Take a short set at the same spot and repeat the same comfortable bend.
knees.evaluation: Compare how similar the bend looks across the set and record makes separately.
knees.source: USA Basketball — 7 Tips To Improve Your Shooting Mechanics

arm.principle: The shooting hand and arm guide the ball on delivery.
arm.cue: Lift the ball with your shooting hand underneath and let the arm extend toward the basket.
arm.purpose: Give the ball a repeatable lift.
arm.avoid_when: When chasing a specific joint angle or changing an effective shot for appearance.
arm.progression: Take a short set close to the rim, then add your guide hand.
arm.evaluation: Compare the shooting arm at similar points in each clip.
arm.source: Jr. NBA — At Home shooting drills

timing.principle: The lower body and shooting arm can work together as one smooth movement.
timing.cue: As you rise, let the ball rise with you in one smooth motion.
timing.purpose: Find a rhythm that is easy to repeat.
timing.use_when: When the shot feels rushed or has an unwanted pause.
timing.avoid_when: When an individualized rhythm is effective and comfortable.
timing.progression: Start close and take a short set from the same spot with one rhythm cue.
timing.evaluation: Check how repeatable the setup-to-release timing looks.
timing.source: USA Basketball — 7 Tips To Improve Your Shooting Mechanics

release.principle: A relaxed shooting wrist is a useful release cue.
release.cue: Finish the lift by letting the ball roll off your fingers toward the rim.
release.purpose: Practice a repeatable finish with the shooting hand.
release.avoid_when: When the player has wrist pain or when estimating trajectory from an elbow angle.
release.progression: Take a short set close to the hoop with the same starting position.
release.evaluation: Check your wrist finish across reps and record makes separately.
release.source: USA Basketball — 7 Tips To Improve Your Shooting Mechanics

finish.principle: A repeatable finish gives you something easy to check after each shot.
finish.cue: Let your shooting arm finish up with your wrist relaxed.
finish.purpose: Make the end of the shooting motion easy to repeat.
finish.use_when: When testing an early finish cue.
finish.avoid_when: When the video ends at release or when interpreting early extension as hold duration.
finish.progression: Take a short set from one spot and think only about the finish.
finish.evaluation: Review early follow-through across the next clips and log makes separately.
finish.source: USA Basketball — 7 Tips To Improve Your Shooting Mechanics

landing.principle: A balanced landing can help you finish under control.
landing.cue: On a stationary jump shot, try landing softly and balanced near your takeoff spot.
landing.purpose: Use a controllable finish in a stationary drill.
landing.avoid_when: When momentum is part of the drill or feet are out of frame.
landing.progression: Start close and record your feet from setup through landing.
landing.evaluation: Review whether you finish balanced from rep to rep.
landing.source: USA Basketball — 7 Tips To Improve Your Shooting Mechanics

distance.principle: Release conditions can change with distance. Compare shots from the same spot first.
distance.cue: Move closer until you can send the ball up comfortably with a smooth release.
distance.purpose: Find a comfortable range for a controlled practice set.
distance.use_when: When a player is exploring range.
distance.avoid_when: When claiming launch angle, speed or power from a joint angle or one missed shot.
distance.progression: Choose one spot for the set. Change distance in the next set only.
distance.evaluation: Log makes, misses and any visible short or long tendency separately at each spot.
distance.source: Slegers, Lee and Wong — Basketball release variability and distance

routine.principle: One repeatable routine gives you a clear starting point for practice.
routine.cue: Set your feet, pick a spot on the rim, then use the same comfortable rhythm each time.
routine.purpose: Give each attempt a similar setup.
routine.use_when: For a beginner or a baseline practice set.
routine.avoid_when: When adding a new sequence would conflict with a reliable existing routine.
routine.progression: Take a short set from one spot. Use the same routine for each shot.
routine.evaluation: Record makes and misses separately from how repeatable your setup-to-release rhythm felt.
routine.source: Jr. NBA — At Home shooting drills

individual.principle: Different players can make effective shots with different comfortable mechanics.
individual.cue: Keep the parts that feel comfortable and work. Test one small change only if it serves your goal.
individual.purpose: Preserve an effective routine while learning what is repeatable.
individual.use_when: When appearance is the main concern.
individual.avoid_when: When a painful movement needs qualified assessment.
individual.progression: Take a set with your usual shot from your usual distance.
individual.evaluation: Compare outcome counts and repeatability across comparable sets.
individual.source: Slegers, Lee and Wong — Basketball release variability and distance

recording.principle: A steady side view with the whole body visible makes pose review easier.
recording.cue: Place the camera on a steady support and keep your feet, shooting hand and hoop in frame.
recording.purpose: Reduce occlusion and make clips easier to compare.
recording.use_when: When clips are hard to interpret or compare.
recording.avoid_when: When treating camera visibility as proof that a measurement is correct.
recording.progression: Record the next set from the same position in good light.
recording.evaluation: Check that setup, release and finish are visible across the set.

safety.principle: Pain that worsens or persists warrants assessment by a qualified healthcare professional.
safety.cue: Pause the shooting movement that makes the pain worse.
safety.use_when: When the player reports pain or injury.
safety.avoid_when: Technique experiments intended to diagnose or treat pain.
